metadata.note: The Texas Midland Railroad (Hetty Green's road, run by her son E.H.R. 'Ned' Green from Terrell): Ennis - Kaufman - Terrell - Greenville - Commerce - Paris, about 124 mi, 1893 until the Southern Pacific purchase of 1 Apr 1928; its Texas & New Orleans (Southern Pacific) years after that; and its predecessor, the Texas Central Railway's northeast branch (one anchor year, 1892). Drawn from the research report research/branches/texas_midland_railroad.txt (historical-trains repo, researched 2026-11-23), converted 2026-11-23. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn. Features are split at every operator change (Texas Central -> TM in 1893, TM -> T&NO in 1928) and at the two Greenville - Commerce track changes (Cotton Belt rights -> own line Nov 1921). The 30 Jun 1934 merger of the TM into the T&NO did not change who ran the trains and is not a split.
sources: John Fowler, Texas Railroads (1) - Passenger Stations & Stops (SL 261), table 88 Paris - Ennis: https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/texasrrs1.pdf

Official Guide Feb 1952 (schedules of 30 Sep 1951), SP Texas Lines Table 80 'Paris and Kaufman' and station index (Enloe, Howland, Harlow daggered 'For freight only'); research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt in the historical-trains repo
metadata.not_yet_sourced: OPEN END: T&NO Commerce - Paris is drawn to 1936, the last CONFIRMED passenger year (July 1936 trade-press article); the real end lies between 1936 and 30 Sep 1951 (freight-only in the Feb 1952 Official Guide). OPEN STARTS (first confirmed year, not opening): TM Ennis - Midland Jct from 1902 (built c.1893/94, undated); TM Roberts - Greenville from 1896 (built 1895). ANCHORS: T&NO Greenville - Commerce own line 1928 only (probably ran to the 1933 abandonment); T&NO Ennis - Greenville 1928 only, with an open end (Ennis - Kaufman no later than the 1942 abandonment; Kaufman - Greenville before Sept 1951); Texas Central Garrett - Roberts 1892 only (service 1882/84-1892 undated). All headways and speeds are estimates. Best leads: T&NO Paris Subdivision employee timetable no. 35 (1942) on tnorr.com; Railroad Commission of Texas annual reports 1931-1939; Portal to Texas History newspapers. SOURCE CONFLICTS recorded: Commerce - Paris opening 1897 (TSHA, Wikipedia, Fowler) vs 1896 (txrrhistory) vs Cooper reached 1895 (THC marker); conveyance to the TM 27 Jan vs 25 Feb 1893; Cooper marker's 'operations ceased in 1934' vs the 1936 Paris motor car; 'Midland Junction' at Garrett (Fowler) vs at Roberts (Wikipedia) - Fowler followed.
metadata.branches_deliberately_omitted: T&NO Commerce - Greenville over the Cotton Belt after the 1933 abandonment of the own line (report block [9]): drawable NONE - no source shows any T&NO passenger train south of Paris/Commerce after 1933; Table 80's title 'Paris and Kaufman' is not dated evidence. Also not drawn: the original Midland Junction - Garrett stub on the TM features (no surviving grade; not the passenger route once the Ennis connection existed) - it appears only as a labelled straight leg on the 1892 Texas Central anchor.
metadata.freight_only_excluded: Every freight-only year after the unknown T&NO passenger end: Kaufman - Greenville to the 1958 lifting, Commerce - Paris to the 1971 floods and 1972/1975 abandonment (including the 1971 Campbell Soup 'Dodger' freight), the TM's Paris industry spur, the Terrell yard spurs and the post-1958 Commerce stub. No T&NO/SP feature is drawn to 1951, 1958, 1971 or 1975.
metadata.horsecar: None; the line was steam from its construction in 1882.
metadata.colour_choice: Texas Midland #5680BF and Texas Central Railway #95BF56 are new; neither company had a feature in data/ and neither hex was used by any company in data/ on 2026-11-23 (checked programmatically, chosen for maximum distance from all existing hexes). Texas & New Orleans features reuse #C1272D, pulled programmatically from data/houston_texas_central.geojson id 'sunbeam-heavyweight' with its exact company string; every Southern Pacific and T&NO feature in data/ was verified to carry the same hex (the one exception, 'Chicago, Rock Island & Pacific / Southern Pacific (joint)' #ffb703, is a joint-company string and is flagged in the research report for the Rock Island cycle). The Texas Central northeast branch is NOT given the Houston and Texas Central colour #9B2226: it was chartered by H&TC interests in 1879, but the one drawn year, 1892, falls after the 1891 foreclosure and reorganization, when the Texas Central was no longer run as part of the H&TC (which was by then under Southern Pacific control), and the branch was sold separately to Hetty Green that October. The 1892 operator is therefore treated as its own company.

properties.geometry_quality: 49.8 mi traced Midland Junction - Crisp - Rosser - Scurry - Kaufman - Terrell - Roberts against 49.8 mi documented (Fowler table 88, Roberts mp 70.5 to Midland Junction mp 120.3; TSHA 51 mi, Wikipedia about 52). No straight-line leg. 14.3 mi on plain railway=abandoned OSM ways with no operator tag (ways 652087313, 1254445259 - the lifted 1942 grade out of Ennis), 11.5 mi on OpenHistoricalMap ways named Texas Central Railroad (OHM ways 202451585 and 202451543, Ennis - Rosser - Kaufman) where OSM has nothing, and 24.0 mi on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=SP (abandoned / razed; e.g. 929497265 Kaufman - Terrell, 103400327 Terrell - Quinlan). Traced mileposts from Paris match Fowler: Roberts 70.3 (70.5), Midland Junction 120.1 (120.3). Midland Junction is taken as the fork where the lifted grade meets the Ennis connection (32.380 N, 96.627 W), per Fowler's reading (near Garrett), NOT Wikipedia's (Roberts). Through Kaufman the trace uses an SP-tagged abandoned way that also carried the T&NO Kemp line; same track, not a different railroad. Not drawn: the original 1882-c.1893 stub from Midland Junction west to the H&TC at Garrett (about 1.9 mi, no surviving grade in OSM or OHM) - after the Ennis connection it was not the passenger route, and before it the TM trains' exact Garrett arrangement is not established.

segments.note: The original Texas Central 'northeast branch' (opened Garrett - Terrell 1882, to Roberts by 1884), taken over by the Texas Midland on 25 Feb 1893 (Galveston Daily News 28 Feb 1893, via txrrhistory Tower 131; sources also give 27 Jan 1893 for the conveyance - recorded, not resolved). Fowler marks Prose, Trinity, Sharman (Hetty), Gailesville and Faulkner with the 1893 Texas Travelers' guide, so passenger service in 1893 is confirmed. Drawn to the sale to Southern Pacific on 1 Apr 1928, after which the Texas & New Orleans ran the trains (separate feature). Through cars of the Lone Star Limited (Frisco / TM / H&TC, St. Louis - Paris - Ennis - Houston) used this line (OG ad July 1902); passenger revenue $28,090 in 1895 and $67,869 in 1926 (TSHA). The 'gas-electric cars' TSHA mentions are undated and unattributed to any run. Headway 720 min (two trains each way a day) is NOT SOURCED - an estimate only; no TM timetable frequency was found.
sources: Segment-level: start from the 1893 takeover (Galveston Daily News 28 Feb 1893 quoted on txrrhistory Tower 131) and Fowler's 1893 Texas Travelers' guide citations (table 88); end at the 1 Apr 1928 SP purchase (TSHA). Taken from the 2026-11-23 research report; headway not sourced.

segments.note: The ex-Texas Midland under the Texas and New Orleans (Southern Pacific), which ran the trains from the 1 Apr 1928 purchase (lease; the TM was merged into the T&NO 30 Jun 1934, which did not change the operator). Railway Signaling and Communications, July 1936 (quoted on txrrhistory Tower 79): 'the traffic on the Southern Pacific consists of one freight train in each direction daily and a local passenger train, a light motor' - a passenger motor car at Paris in 1936; the article does not say how far south it ran. 1928-1936 continuity is inferred (TM trains to the sale, SP trains in 1936). OPEN END: 1936 is the LAST CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end - no source dates when passenger service stopped. By 30 Sep 1951 the line was freight-only (Feb 1952 Official Guide, Table 80 'Freight Service only'), so the end lies somewhere in 1936 - 1951. Do not extend without evidence. Freight ran on until the 1971 floods; abandoned 1972 (ICC) or 1975 (TSHA) - not drawn (Rule 1). The Cooper Rail Depot marker's claim that TM operations ceased in 1934 conflicts with the 1936 motor car; recorded, not resolved. Headway 1440 (one motor each way) is an estimate from the 1936 article's 'a local passenger train', not a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: start at the 1 Apr 1928 SP purchase/T&NO lease (TSHA); end 1936 = last confirmed year, Railway Signaling and Communications July 1936 quoted on txrrhistory Tower 79; freight-only by 1951 per the Feb 1952 Official Guide. Headway estimated.
